profiles.experience: Completed a 3-month summer internship working with Node.js backend development.
profiles.projects: E-Commerce full-stack app with basic payment integration and reactive catalog.

profiles.experience: Undergrad data structures researcher and tutor. Developed models for campus admissions analytics.
profiles.projects: Academic performance predictive modeling using random forests and gradient boosted trees.

assessments.title: Two Sum
assessments.description:
Given an array of integers `nums` and an integer `target`, return indices of the two numbers such that they add up to `target`.
You may assume that each input would have exactly one solution, and you may not use the same element twice.

assessments.title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock
assessments.description:
You are given an array `prices` where `prices[i]` is the price of a given stock on the `i`-th day.
You want to maximize your profit by choosing a single day to buy one stock and choosing a different day in the future to sell that stock.
Return the maximum profit you can achieve.

examples.explanation: Buy on day 2 (price = 1) and sell on day 5 (price = 6), profit = 6-1 = 5.

assessments.title: Contains Duplicate
assessments.description: Given an integer array `nums`, return `true` if any value appears at least twice in the array, and return `false` if every element is distinct.

assessments.title: Product of Array Except Self
assessments.description:
Given an integer array `nums`, return an array `answer` such that `answer[i]` is equal to the product of all the elements of `nums` except `nums[i]`.
Write an algorithm that runs in `O(n)` time and without using the division operation.

assessments.title: Maximum Subarray
assessments.description: Given an integer array `nums`, find the subarray with the largest sum, and return its sum.

examples.explanation: The subarray [4,-1,2,1] has the largest sum = 6.

assessments.title: Reverse String
assessments.description:
Write a function that reverses a string. The input string is given as an array of characters `s`.
You must do this by modifying the input array in-place with O(1) extra memory.
constraints: s[i] is a printable ascii character.

assessments.title: Valid Anagram
assessments.description: Given two strings `s` and `t`, return `true` if `t` is an anagram of `s`, and `false` otherwise.
constraints: s and t consist of lowercase English letters.

assessments.title: Valid Palindrome
assessments.description:
A phrase is a palindrome if, after converting all uppercase letters into lowercase letters and removing all non-alphanumeric characters, it reads the same forward and backward.
Given a string `s`, return `true` if it is a palindrome, or `false` otherwise.
constraints: s consists of printable ASCII characters.

examples.input: s = "A man, a plan, a canal: Panama"

testCases.input: ["A man, a plan, a canal: Panama"]

assessments.title: Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters
assessments.description: Given a string `s`, find the length of the longest substring without repeating characters.
constraints: s consists of English letters, digits, symbols and spaces.

examples.explanation: The answer is "abc", with the length of 3.

assessments.title: Group Anagrams
assessments.description: Given an array of strings `strs`, group the anagrams together. You can return the answer in any order.
constraints: strs[i] consists of lowercase English letters.

assessments.title: Reverse Linked List
assessments.description: Given the head of a singly linked list, reverse the list, and return the reversed list.
constraints: The number of nodes in the list is the range [0, 5000].

assessments.title: Merge Two Sorted Lists
assessments.description:
You are given the heads of two sorted linked lists `list1` and `list2`.
Merge the two lists into one sorted list. The list should be made by splicing together the nodes of the first two lists.
constraints: The number of nodes in both lists is in the range [0, 50].
Both list1 and list2 are sorted in non-decreasing order.

assessments.title: Linked List Cycle
assessments.description: Determine if a linked list contains a cycle. Return `true` if there is a cycle in the list, otherwise `false`.
constraints: The number of nodes in the list is in the range [0, 10^4].

assessments.title: Remove Nth Node From End of List
assessments.description: Given the `head` of a linked list, remove the `n`-th node from the end of the list and return its head.
constraints: The number of nodes in the list is sz.

assessments.title: Valid Parentheses
assessments.description: Given a string `s` containing just the characters `(`, `)`, `{`, `}`, `[` and `]`, determine if the input string is valid.

assessments.title: Min Stack
assessments.description:
Design a stack that supports push, pop, top, and retrieving the minimum element in constant time.
Implement the MinStack class.
constraints: Methods will be called at most 3 * 10^4 times.
Pop, top and getMin are always called on non-empty stacks.

assessments.title: Evaluate Reverse Polish Notation
assessments.description: Evaluate the value of an arithmetic expression in Reverse Polish Notation. Valid operators are `+`, `-`, `*`, and `/`.
constraints: tokens[i] is either an operator or an integer.

assessments.title: Daily Temperatures
assessments.description: Given an array of integers `temperatures` representing the daily temperatures, return an array `answer` such that `answer[i]` is the number of days you have to wait after the `i`-th day to get a warmer temperature.

assessments.title: Implement Queue using Stacks
assessments.description: Implement a first in first out (FIFO) queue using only two stacks. The implemented queue should support push, peek, pop, and empty.

assessments.title: Number of Recent Calls
assessments.description: You have a `RecentCounter` class which counts the number of recent requests within a certain time frame.
constraints: Each test case calls ping with strictly increasing values.

assessments.title: Design Circular Queue
assessments.description: Design your implementation of the circular queue. The circular queue is a linear data structure in which the operations are performed based on FIFO principle and the last position is connected back to the first.

assessments.title: Sliding Window Maximum
assessments.description:
You are given an array of integers `nums`, there is a sliding window of size `k` which is moving from the very left of the array to the very right. You can only see the `k` numbers in the window. Each time the sliding window moves right by one position.
Return the max sliding window.

assessments.title: Maximum Depth of Binary Tree
assessments.description:
Given the `root` of a binary tree, return its maximum depth.
A binary tree's maximum depth is the number of nodes along the longest path from the root node down to the farthest leaf node.
constraints: The number of nodes in the tree is in the range [0, 10^4].

assessments.title: Invert Binary Tree
assessments.description: Given the `root` of a binary tree, invert the tree, and return its root.
constraints: The number of nodes in the tree is in the range [0, 100].

assessments.title: Same Tree
assessments.description: Given the roots of two binary trees `p` and `q`, write a function to check if they are the same or not.
constraints: The number of nodes in both trees is in the range [0, 100].

assessments.title: Binary Tree Level Order Traversal
assessments.description: Given the `root` of a binary tree, return the level order traversal of its nodes' values. (i.e., from left to right, level by level).
constraints: The number of nodes in the tree is in the range [0, 2000].

assessments.title: Validate Binary Search Tree
assessments.description: Given the `root` of a binary tree, determine if it is a valid binary search tree (BST).
constraints: The number of nodes in the tree is in the range [1, 10^4].

assessments.title: Find Path in Graph
assessments.description: Given a bi-directed graph with `n` vertices, check if there is a valid path from `source` vertex to `destination` vertex.

assessments.title: Number of Islands
assessments.description: Given an `m x n` 2D binary grid `grid` which represents a map of `1`s (land) and `0`s (water), return the number of islands.

assessments.title: Clone Graph
assessments.description: Given a reference of a node in a connected undirected graph, return a deep copy (clone) of the graph.
constraints: The number of nodes in the graph is between 0 and 100.

assessments.title: Course Schedule
assessments.description:
There are a total of `numCourses` courses you have to take, labeled from `0` to `numCourses - 1`. You are given an array `prerequisites` where `prerequisites[i] = [ai, bi]` indicates that you must take course `bi` first if you want to take course `ai`.
Return `true` if you can finish all courses. Otherwise, return `false`.

assessments.title: Climbing Stairs
assessments.description: You are climbing a staircase. It takes `n` steps to reach the top. Each time you can either climb 1 or 2 steps. In how many distinct ways can you climb to the top?

assessments.title: Coin Change
assessments.description:
You are given an integer array `coins` representing coins of different denominations and an integer `amount` representing a total amount of money.
Return the fewest number of coins that you need to make up that amount. If that amount of money cannot be made up by any combination of the coins, return `-1`.

assessments.title: Longest Increasing Subsequence
assessments.description: Given an integer array `nums`, return the length of the longest strictly increasing subsequence.

examples.explanation: The longest increasing subsequence is [2,3,7,101], length 4.

assessments.title: House Robber
assessments.description:
You are a professional robber planning to rob houses along a street. Each house has a certain amount of money stashed, the only constraint stopping you from robbing each of them is that adjacent houses have security systems connected and it will automatically contact the police if two adjacent houses were broken into on the same night.
Given an integer array `nums` representing the amount of money of each house, return the maximum amount of money you can rob tonight without alerting the police.

examples.explanation: Rob house 1 (money = 1) and then rob house 3 (money = 3). Total amount = 1 + 3 = 4.

assessments.title: Edit Distance
assessments.description:
Given two strings `word1` and `word2`, return the minimum number of operations required to convert `word1` to `word2`.
You have the following three operations permitted on a word: Insert, Delete, Replace.
constraints: word1 and word2 consist of lowercase English letters.

assessments.title: Assign Cookies
assessments.description: Assume you are an awesome parent and want to give your children some cookies. But, you should give each child at most one cookie. Each child i has a greed factor `g[i]`, which is the minimum size of a cookie that the child will be content with; and each cookie j has a size `s[j]`. If `s[j] >= g[i]`, we can assign the cookie j to the child i, and the child i will be content. Your goal is to maximize the number of your content children and output the maximum number.

assessments.title: Jump Game
assessments.description:
You are given an integer array `nums`. You are initially positioned at the array's first index, and each element in the array represents your maximum jump length at that position.
Return `true` if you can reach the last index, or `false` otherwise.

assessments.title: Gas Station
assessments.description:
There are `n` gas stations along a circular route, where the amount of gas at the `i`-th station is `gas[i]`. You have a car with an unlimited gas tank and it costs `cost[i]` of gas to travel from the `i`-th station to its next `(i+1)`-th station. You begin the journey with an empty tank at one of the gas stations.
Given two integer arrays `gas` and `cost`, return the starting gas station's index if you can travel around the circuit once in the clockwise direction, otherwise return `-1`.

assessments.title: Partition Labels
assessments.description:
You are given a string `s`. We want to partition the string into as many parts as possible so that each letter appears in at most one part.
Return a list of integers representing the size of these parts.
constraints: s consists of lowercase English letters.

assessments.title: Non-overlapping Intervals
assessments.description: Given an array of intervals `intervals` where `intervals[i] = [starti, endi]`, return the minimum number of intervals you need to remove to make the rest of the intervals non-overlapping.

assessments.title: Fibonacci Number
assessments.description: The Fibonacci numbers, commonly denoted F(n) form a sequence, called the Fibonacci sequence, such that each number is the sum of the two preceding ones, starting from 0 and 1.

assessments.title: Subsets
assessments.description: Given an integer array `nums` of unique elements, return all possible subsets (the power set). The solution set must not contain duplicate subsets. Return the solution in any order.

assessments.title: Permutations
assessments.description: Given an array `nums` of distinct integers, return all the possible permutations. You can return the answer in any order.
constraints: All integers in nums are distinct.

assessments.title: Generate Parentheses
assessments.description: Given `n` pairs of parentheses, write a function to generate all combinations of well-formed parentheses.

assessments.title: Merge Sorted Array
assessments.description:
You are given two integer arrays `nums1` and `nums2`, sorted in non-decreasing order, and two integers `m` and `n`, representing the number of elements in `nums1` and `nums2` respectively.
Merge `nums1` and `nums2` into a single array sorted in non-decreasing order in-place in `nums1`.

assessments.title: Sort Colors
assessments.description:
Given an array `nums` with `n` objects colored red, white, or blue, sort them in-place so that objects of the same color are adjacent, with the colors in the order red, white, and blue.
We will use the integers 0, 1, and 2 to represent the colors red, white, and blue, respectively.

assessments.title: Kth Largest Element in an Array
assessments.description: Given an integer array `nums` and an integer `k`, return the `k`-th largest element in the array.

assessments.title: Top K Frequent Elements
assessments.description: Given an integer array `nums` and an integer `k`, return the `k` most frequent elements. You may return the answer in any order.
constraints: k is in the range [1, the number of unique elements in the array].
It is guaranteed that the answer is unique.

assessments.title: Binary Search
assessments.description: Given an array of integers `nums` which is sorted in ascending order, and an integer `target`, write a function to search `target` in `nums`. If `target` exists, then return its index. Otherwise, return `-1`.
constraints: All the integers in nums are unique.
nums is sorted in ascending order.

assessments.title: Search in Rotated Sorted Array
assessments.description:
There is an integer array `nums` sorted in ascending order (with distinct values).
Given the array `nums` after the possible rotation and an integer `target`, return the index of `target` if it is in `nums`, or `-1` if it is not in `nums`.
constraints: All values of nums are unique.

assessments.title: Find Minimum in Rotated Sorted Array
assessments.description: Suppose an array of length `n` sorted in ascending order is rotated between `1` and `n` times. Given the sorted rotated array `nums` of unique elements, return the minimum element of this array.
constraints: All the integers in nums are unique.

assessments.title: Merge Intervals
assessments.description: Given an array of `intervals` where `intervals[i] = [start_i, end_i]`, merge all overlapping intervals, and return an array of the non-overlapping intervals that cover all the intervals in the input.

assessments.title: Container With Most Water
assessments.description: You are given an integer array `height` of length `n`. Find two lines that together with the x-axis form a container, such that the container contains the most water. Return the maximum amount of water a container can store.

assessments.title: Longest Palindromic Substring
assessments.description: Given a string `s`, return the longest palindromic substring in `s`.
constraints: s elements consist of Digits and English letters.

assessments.title: String to Integer (atoi)
assessments.description: Implement the `myAtoi(string s)` function, which converts a string to a 32-bit signed integer (similar to C/C++'s atoi function).

assessments.title: Add Two Numbers
assessments.description: You are given two non-empty linked lists representing two non-negative integers. The digits are stored in reverse order, and each of their nodes contains a single digit. Add the two numbers and return the sum as a linked list.
constraints: The number of nodes in each linked list is in the range [1, 100].

assessments.title: Next Greater Element I
assessments.description: The next greater element of some element x in an array is the first greater element to its right. Find all next greater elements.

assessments.title: Simplify Path
assessments.description: Given an absolute path for a Unix-style file system, simplify it to the canonical path.

assessments.title: Task Scheduler
assessments.description: Given a characters array `tasks`, representing the tasks a CPU needs to do, and a cooling time `n`, return the least number of units of times that the CPU will take to finish all the given tasks.

assessments.title: Path Sum
assessments.description: Given the `root` of a binary tree and an integer `targetSum`, return `true` if the tree has a root-to-leaf path such that adding up all the values along the path equals `targetSum`.
constraints: Number of nodes is in range [0, 5000].

assessments.title: Lowest Common Ancestor of a Binary Tree
assessments.description: Given a binary tree, find the lowest common ancestor (LCA) of two given nodes in the tree.
constraints: Number of nodes is in range [2, 10^5].

assessments.title: Redundant Connection
assessments.description: In this problem, a tree is an undirected graph that is connected and has no cycles. Return an edge that can be removed so that the resulting graph is a tree of n nodes.

assessments.title: Network Delay Time
assessments.description: You are given a network of `n` nodes, labeled from `1` to `n`. You are also given `times`, a list of travel times as directed edges. Return the minimum time it takes for all the nodes to receive the signal.

assessments.title: Longest Palindromic Subsequence
assessments.description: Given a string `s`, find the longest palindromic subsequence's length in `s`.

assessments.title: Unique Paths
assessments.description: There is a robot on an `m x n` grid. The robot is initially located at the top-left corner. The robot tries to move to the bottom-right corner. The robot can only move either down or right at any point in time.

assessments.title: Longest Common Subsequence
assessments.description: Given two strings `text1` and `text2`, return the length of their longest common subsequence. If there is no common subsequence, return 0.

assessments.title: Queue Reconstruction by Height
assessments.description: You are given an array of people, `people`, which are the attributes of some people in a queue (not necessarily in order). Reconstruct and return the queue.

assessments.title: Minimum Number of Arrows to Burst Balloons
assessments.description: There are some spherical balloons taped onto a flat wall that represents the XY-plane. Find the minimum number of arrows that must be shot to burst all balloons.

assessments.title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock II
assessments.description: You are given an integer array `prices` where `prices[i]` is the price of a given stock on the `i`-th day. Find the maximum profit you can achieve.

assessments.title: Combinations
assessments.description: Given two integers `n` and `k`, return all possible combinations of `k` numbers chosen from the range `[1, n]`.

assessments.title: Combination Sum
assessments.description: Given an array of distinct integers `candidates` and a target integer `target`, return a list of all unique combinations of candidates where the chosen numbers sum to target.

assessments.title: Sort an Array
assessments.description: Given an array of integers `nums`, sort the array in ascending order and return it.

assessments.title: Largest Number
assessments.description: Given a list of non-negative integers `nums`, arrange them such that they form the largest number and return it.

assessments.title: Search a 2D Matrix
assessments.description: You are given an `m x n` integer matrix `matrix` which is sorted: integers in each row are sorted from left to right, and the first integer of each row is greater than the last integer of the previous row. Return true if target is in the matrix.

assessments.title: First and Last Position of Element
assessments.description: Given an array of integers `nums` sorted in non-decreasing order, find the starting and ending position of a given `target` value. If target is not found in the array, return `[-1, -1]`.

messages.content: Welcome Rikhil. Tell me, how do you manage state and avoid excess re-rendering in a large-scale React app?

I split the component hierarchy and use local state by default. For global state, I use React Context, with memoized hooks or specialized state stores like Zustand, taking care to place keys correctly in dependency arrays.
That makes perfect sense. How would you handle errors on a Node API when a third-party payment provider goes offline?

I would set robust try-catch blocks, implement a retry mechanism with exponential backoff, and log the precise error context securely. I would return an appropriate user-facing warning with an HTTP 503 code so the client UI can suggest retrying shortly.
